Description:
Why Louis & Jean Pannullo chose Chatham

We choose Chatham because we have been coming here for years. There is so much to do and see here. Great boutiques and antique shops, wonderful restaurants, Chatham Angler games, biking and fantastic beaches. We searched a long time to find the right house for us. All houses with seven foot ceiling were immediately out of the running. We wanted a house filled with light with room enough for our large extended family. This property charmed us from the get go with its beautifully landscaped grounds, expansive floor plan, great location and overall good feel. We have enjoyed furnishing the house from top to bottom seeking out those special items that add a little zing. From a spinning authentic captains wheel coffee table, to a big metal fish hanging from the two story sunroom from a tackle this house is filled with special touches that make a house a home. We especially enjoy the two private decks and the public deck that runs along the sunroom, living room and dining room. This house is an indoor/outdoor haven. It also has a private entrance to the family room, basement King bedroom which has its own kitchenette and full bathroom. The home offers 5 bedrooms in 2 separate living spaces with separate entrances. Keyless entry is provided for convenience. Chatham Beach Cruiser has a media room and an outdoor deck with a Bose speaker system. A stainless steel barbecue is available for use.

Activities nearby include golf, bike trails and antique shopping. Scatteree Beach is within walking distance.

Chatham Light Beach is 3.3 km from the property, while the Chatham Shark Center is 650 metres away. The nearest airport is Nantucket Memorial Airport, 50 km from the property. Known locally as Star of the Sea, HI Nantucket was built as a lifesaving station in 1873 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The lookout station, or cupola, is still accessible from the womens dormitory, and the hostel is just minutes away from Surfside Beach and only 3.5 miles from the ferry docks and Nantucket village. This Nantucket hostel has a fully equipped kitchen for preparing your own meals, a large dining area, outdoor picnic tables and bicycle racks. Breakfast, Wi-Fi access and parking are free. The hostel also has one of the few sand volleyball courts on the island! From the hostel guests can take the bike path into town and check out the Whaling Museum to learn about the islands fascinating past. Description:
At Heart of It All! Lotus Provincetown is located in the center of town, just steps from where the ferry lands on the picturesque wharf filled with charming boats and tiny seaside shops. Within less than a minute walk on Commercial Street, visitors are treated to the delicious treats at the famous Portuguese Bakery, the tantalizing shows at the Post Office Cabaret, succulent seafood at the renowned Lobster Pot, and many, many more offerings from Provinctowns most notable institutions.

Lotus Provinctown first opened in the 1980s by the Lovingers, who lovingly restored the Queen Anne building originally known as the Cutler Pharmacy when it was built around 1900. The building underwent a full renovation in 2008, and its current owner has further modernized the property with remote locks for contactless checkins, streaming TVs, and all white, luxurious down bedding. The property has a charming, private garden hidden from busy Commercial Street, housing a cedar tub, dry sauna, and outdoor shower (beginning June 2023).

Lotus Provincetown is located in the heart of the historic district. Youre just a few feet away from restaurants, galleries, shops, bars and clubs. And when you just want to relax, the beach is just a few yards away for a walk to see the the boats and the sunset. Guests are required to show a photo identification and credit card upon check-in. Description:
The Tucker Inn is one of a handful of stately 2nd Empire Victorian Cottages found in Provincetown. Built in 1872 at the height of the whaling fortunes, it possesses the charm and intricacy of detail of that golden era. We keep the house gently restored, updating while retaining its heart in an earlier era.

We are a true bed and breakfast inn and our breakfasts go far beyond the ordinary: we offer what may be the best breakfast in Provincetown. Each morning our chef whips up another mouth-watering creation. We call it an eclectic international cuisine. Belgian Waffles, Greek Omelets, Breakfast Quesadillas assure that you start each day of your vacation with a little happiness.

The house may be historic but our services arent: you can keep in touch through high speed internet, or you can veg out in the hot tub, or chill out in the meditation garden or in the new relaxation garden.

Our mission is to give you a chance to relax and rejuvenate. Were not into attitude here. Our guests are men and women, mostly-but-not-all gay, sometimes children and sometimes dogs. Built in 1872, The Tucker Inn is a pet-friendly Victorian-era accommodation in Provincetown. A full breakfast is provided daily, and the property offers free WiFi.

All rooms are air-conditioned and have a small refrigerator and flat-screen TV. Rooms are equipped with a hairdryer and bathrobes.

Guests can relax in the hot tub or make use of the Zen garden for meditation.
